analysis.title: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) Q3'26 Review: Mgmt Frames Forward Narratives (AWS Revenue Growth; Operating Margin Trajectory) Key to Long-Term Fundamentals; Compelling Risk/Reward from Current Levels
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on AMZN and lowers the 12-month price target to $370 from $375, which is 51.8% above the $243.79 close on 29 Oct 2026. At the after-hours price of $225 the stock trades at about 20x GS 2027 GAAP EPS.
Q3'26 AWS revenue grew 39% and segment GAAP operating margin was 39%. Both beat GSe/Street estimates but came in below some buyside expectations.

Management framed AWS demand as capacity constrained. Backlog reached $578B (+189% YoY), AI revenue is growing triple digits, and management projects AWS revenue growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. Capacity is largely sold out for the next 2 years.
Management expects AWS to reach a $1tn annual revenue run rate eventually.

Custom silicon volumes grew more than 20x YoY. Customers reportedly saved $2b in the quarter using AMZN silicon, management cited 30-40% better price-performance, and AMZN announced an opportunity to sell Trainium externally in 2H27.
Commerce margins continue to improve, with multi-year tailwinds from automation, robotics and inventory optimization. AMZN is on track to cut cost to serve per unit for the 4th consecutive year.
Management expressed rising confidence in the ROIC of AI capital investment, citing accelerating capex payback periods and demand curves.
Fresh grocery and everyday essentials are about half of all units sold. Grocery customers shop 4x more and spend 2x more than non-grocery customers.

Q3'26 advertising was 4-6% below GSe/Street, with a ~850bps headwind from the timing shift of Prime Day and NBA. Management expects high-teens advertising growth in 4Q and cited Prime Video run-rate revenue in the tens of billions of dollars.
Q4'26 GAAP operating income guidance is about 3-6% below GSe/Street at the midpoint, partly because Leo capitalization costs are now expected in 2027.

GS notes investor anchoring on capex needs beyond 2027, how the build-out is funded, and possible operating volatility from the evolution of web 2.0 businesses. GS sees GAAP operating income as a 33% CAGR from 2026 to 2030.
GS models negative free cash flow of -$60.7bn in 2026E, -$61.7bn in 2027E and -$24.3bn in 2028E, with capex of $220.3bn, $326.1bn and $366.9bn in those years.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees AWS demand outstripping supply, commerce margins expanding and advertising scaling, with AMZN at about 20x 2027 GAAP EPS. The PT cut reflects lower SOTP multiples.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported total revenue was $201,944mm vs GS $201,505mm and consensus $202,346mm, against guidance of $197-202bn.
Q3'26 reported GAAP operating income was $28,076mm vs GS $26,037mm and consensus $26,163mm, against guidance of $22.5-26.5bn. Margin was 13.9% vs 12.9% for both GS and consensus.
Q3'26 reported AWS revenue was $45,984mm vs GS $46,703mm and consensus $45,445mm, so -1.5% vs GS and +1.2% vs consensus. Growth was 39% YoY.
Q3'26 reported advertising services revenue was $19,637mm vs GS $20,535mm and consensus $20,879mm, so -4.4% vs GS and -5.9% vs consensus.
Q3'26 reported North America sales were $112,852mm vs consensus $113,791mm. International sales were $43,108mm vs consensus $43,011mm.
GS Q4'26 estimates (new vs old): revenue $242.68bn (from $241.43bn), GAAP EBIT $31.94bn (from $32.02bn), GAAP EPS $2.29 (from $2.33).
GS 2027 estimates (new vs old): revenue $964.06bn (from $962.38bn), GAAP EBIT $156.15bn (from $152.25bn), GAAP EPS $11.18 (from $10.99).
GS FY26 diluted EPS estimate is $12.67 (old $12.76), which benefits from other income of $53.4bn reported in Q2. GS FY28 EPS estimate is $14.81 (old $14.02).
Q4'26 AWS revenue estimate is unchanged at $51,234mm, and GS 2028 AWS revenue estimate rises 5% to $336,370mm.
risk_factors: Competition reducing eCommerce or cloud growth.
Failure to scale high-margin businesses: advertising, cloud, third-party selling and subscriptions.
Investment across initiatives pressuring gross or operating margin.
Product or platform changes needed to comply with global regulation.
Global macro volatility and weaker investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
Capital requirements and return profile, and a possible negative impact from agentic commerce.
Free cash flow is negative through 2028E in GS estimates, and long-term debt is modeled rising to $204bn in 2026E from $66bn.
vol_and_positioning: GS says investors are increasingly anchored on questions about sustained capex beyond 2027 and the sources of capital to fund the build-out.

AMZN returned 7.6% over 3 months, -7.3% over 6 months and 5.9% over 12 months in absolute terms, versus the S&P 500 at +1.6%, -14.6% and -5.8% relative. These relative figures are as printed in the price performance table.

tension_points.bull_case: AWS backlog of $578B, capacity largely sold out for 2 years, projected AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028, and accelerating capex payback periods support the AI investment.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors question sustained capex beyond 2027, how the build-out is funded, and returns. GS models negative free cash flow through 2028E and a rise in long-term debt. The 39% AWS growth also fell short of some buyside expectations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown in AWS growth below the projected 40%-plus in 2027 and 2028, or capital requirements and return profile worse than GS models.
